subject: MAP check-in: performance benchmark results, tuning plan & next checkpoint
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP check-in: performance benchmark results, tuning plan & next checkpoint

Hi Jordan —

Following up on our MAP milestones for the performance eval: we completed the end-to-end benchmark runs against your staging traces last Friday. Summary attached (redwood_map_perf_summary_v3.pdf) and TL;DR below.

Key findings (staging config: rtx-8000 x4, batch target 8, seq=1024):
- 95th latency: ~210 ms per request (baseline run)
- 99th latency: ~360 ms (spikes correlated with long sequences and cold KV cache)
- Sustained throughput: ~120k tokens/min across the pool (≈120 tokens/s per GPU under steady-state)

Notes: we saw periodic latency spikes during burst windows when many small requests arrive simultaneously (batching threshold behavior). Marcus included raw run logs for triage.

Proposed next steps for the MAP (short list):
- Enable prefix-based KV caching for repeated prompts (owner: Marcus)
- Adjust dynamic batching policy to reduce small-request amplification (owner: Karthik)
- Run small canary with quantized weights (8-bit) to validate accuracy impact (owner: Mina + Acme)

Can we schedule a 30-min checkpoint next Tuesday to review tuning outcomes and update the mutual action plan? I attached the perf PDF and will add the action tracker after we align.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment: redwood_map_perf_summary_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.2 MB)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP check-in: performance benchmark results, tuning plan & next checkpoint

Thanks Mina — this is really helpful. Quick clarifications before the call:
- Can you break out p50/p95/p99 by request size buckets (<=128 tokens, 129-512, 513-1024)? Our production mix skews small.
- For throughput, did you observe GPU saturation or CPU/IO bottlenecks during the bursts?

We've attached a short load profile from our side (acme_load_profile.csv) to help match the runs. If possible, can Marcus or Karthik call out the expected accuracy delta for the 8-bit canary? We need that to sign off on the canary schedule.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Lead ML Platform Engineer, Acme Health
jordan.lee@acmehealth.com | +1 617-555-0137

Attachment: acme_load_profile.csv (csv, 24 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP check-in: performance benchmark results, tuning plan & next checkpoint

Adding details from the raw runs (see perf_run_20270611.log):
- p50 by bucket: <=128: 45 ms | 129-512: 110 ms | 513-1024: 180 ms
- p95 by bucket: <=128: 95 ms | 129-512: 210 ms | 513-1024: 320 ms
- p99 by bucket: <=128: 160 ms | 129-512: 330 ms | 513-1024: 520 ms
- Observed tail spikes align with KV cache cold starts and when dynamic batching drops below batch threshold for small requests.

Throughput notes: GPU utilization hit ~82% during steady-state; CPU IO waits spiked briefly during the burst period (we're seeing protobuf deserialization overhead on the worker side).

Immediate mitigations I recommend for the MAP sprint:
1) Lower batching trigger for small requests from 6 -> 3 to reduce queuing latency (canary on dedicated staging pool) — owner: Karthik — target: 2 business days
2) Prefetch KV segments for top-100 prompts (reduces cold-cache misses) — owner: Marcus — target: 3 business days
3) Run 8-bit quantized model on 1 node (compare eval metric delta using existing eval suite) — owner: Mina + Acme — target: 5 business days

I've attached the raw log for diagnostic.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: perf_run_20270611.log (log, 320 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP check-in: performance benchmark results, tuning plan & next checkpoint

Agree with Marcus' triage. A couple of implementation notes for the MAP tuning tasks:
- Batching policy change: we'll roll out a config flag in the staging fleet to lower small-request threshold and enable micro-batching for short sequences. I'll instrument per-route latency so we can measure impact within 24 hrs. (Owner: Karthik)
- KV prefetch: will add a warm-up hook for the top-100 predicted prefixes. We'll monitor memory footprint — estimate +6% RAM usage for 100 prefixes. (Owner: Marcus)
- Quantization canary: recommend A/B on 5% of traffic in staging with strict automated evals on our eval harness (prompt_set/map_eval_v2). If eval delta < 0.5% on your primary metrics, we can proceed to a larger canary. (Owners: Mina + Jordan)

Action item owners and rough due dates in-message:
- Karthik: batching config change (staging canary) — due: 2027-06-18
- Marcus: KV prefetch implementation & mem monitor — due: 2027-06-20
- Mina + Jordan: 8-bit canary plan & eval criteria — due: 2027-06-18

I'll instrument extra logs for the small request path to capture batching decisions.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: MAP checkpoint notes & action tracker (perf tuning) — next checkpoint 2027-06-24

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick turn. Recap from our sync and the agreed MAP actions below; I've also attached the MAP_action_tracker.xlsx with owners, JIRA refs, and status.

Meeting summary:
- Benchmarks validated Marcus' observations: small-request tails are the primary source of p99 spikes; KV cold starts and batching thresholds are contributors.
- Agreed canary plan for 8-bit quantization with strict eval gates; Acme to review accuracy thresholds defined in the tracker.

Action items (owners / due dates):
- Karthik: roll out batching threshold change to staging and enable per-route latency charts — due 2027-06-18 — JIRA RDW-PLAT-789
- Marcus: implement KV prefetch warm-up hook for top-100 prefixes, add memory monitor — due 2027-06-20 — JIRA RDW-ENG-1024
- Mina + Jordan: finalize 8-bit canary eval criteria and start canary run (5% traffic) — due 2027-06-18 — tracker attached
- Mina: update MAP in HubSpot with these milestones and timing — due 2027-06-21 — HubSpot link in tracker

Next checkpoint: Thu, 24 Jun 2027, 11:00 AM PT — 30 min to review canary results and update close timeline. Please confirm availability; if anything slips, flag in the tracker so we can adjust the MAP dates.

Thanks all — pulling items into the MAP_action_tracker.xlsx and HubSpot now.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
